title: US Judge Dismisses Criminal Charges Against Gautam Adani After DOJ Abandons Bribery Case
excerpt: Brooklyn federal judge grants rare DOJ request to drop 2024 fraud and bribery indictment, ending a high-profile prosecution that spanned two presidential administrations.
body:
• US District Judge Nicholas Garaufis dismissed all criminal charges against Gautam Adani on Monday after the Justice Department moved to abandon the case.
  • The DOJ under Trump called the Biden-era indictment a "foreign case" with little chance of success, describing it as a "name and shame" action.
  • Adani was charged in 2024 with agreeing to bribe Indian officials to win solar energy approvals and misleading US investors about anti-corruption practices.
  • The judge had initially pushed back, calling the DOJ's reasoning "bland and conclusory," before ultimately granting dismissal after further justification.

Judge Grants Rare Dismissal

A US federal judge on Monday dismissed criminal charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, closing out a case that had cast a shadow over one of Asia's largest conglomerates for nearly two years.

https://x.com/KommawarSwapnil/status/2087039421350846806

Brooklyn-based US District Judge Nicholas Garaufis granted the Justice Department's request to drop the fraud and bribery case — but not before probing prosecutors' reasons for doing so, including asking Adani whether anything was promised in exchange for the charges being dropped, according to Reuters.

"The Government's terse, bland and conclusory statement affords the court neither a sufficient basis to reach any conclusion, nor the opportunity to conduct any analysis of the Government's request for dismissal."

— Judge Nicholas Garaufis, in an earlier ruling questioning the DOJ's initial request

How the Case Unraveled

Adani was charged in 2024 with agreeing to bribe Indian government officials so a subsidiary of his Adani Group could win approval to develop a solar energy plant, then misleading US investors by providing reassuring information about his company's anti-corruption practices. The charges were unsealed in November 2024, during the final days of the Biden administration.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=jHMcKc9W7KQ

The Adani Group has consistently denied wrongdoing. Adani himself never appeared in US court to respond to the charges.

On May 18, the Justice Department under President Trump announced it would no longer pursue the case — the latest in a series of high-profile white-collar prosecutions dropped during Trump's second term. But legal experts noted that charges cannot be formally dismissed without a judge's approval.

Garaufis initially refused to rubber-stamp the dismissal, ordering prosecutors to explain their reasoning. In a July 4 filing, senior DOJ official Trent McCotter responded with a 10-page brief arguing that the case was primarily foreign, difficult to prove, and inconsistent with the agency's current priorities.

DOJ Calls Biden-Era Case a 'Name and Shame'

McCotter's filing cast the original prosecution as politically motivated. "The indictment was unsealed in the final days of the prior Administration, apparently as a 'name and shame' designed to levy accusations without any realistic prospect of a trial ever occurring," the filing stated.

The DOJ argued that US government attorneys should not prosecute a "foreign case" involving alleged conduct by Indian nationals, working for Indian companies, paying the Indian government, with "no U.S. interests implicated in any way."

Brooklyn US Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said in a separate letter that he was "not the decisionmaker" behind dropping the case but had no basis to challenge McCotter's reasoning.

Impact on Adani Group

Adani Group stocks are expected to gain following the dismissal, according to Reuters. The conglomerate — which spans ports, airports, energy, and mining — had seen its market value battered after the 2024 indictment compounded pressure from the Hindenburg Research short-seller report that preceded it in January 2023.

Before the charges were unsealed, Adani had promised to invest $10 billion in the United States. The timeline of that commitment and the DOJ's decision to drop charges raised questions about whether the two were connected — a point Judge Garaufis explored directly in Monday's hearing.

What's Next

While the criminal case is now closed, Adani still faces a civil lawsuit from the US Securities and Exchange Commission over the same alleged bribery scheme. The SEC sued Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani in November 2024, alleging they misled investors in a 2021 bond sale by the group's renewable energy arm, Adani Green Energy Ltd. That case remains active.

Airbus confirmed Monday it is sending specialists to India for a separate investigation — unrelated to Adani — underscoring a busy day for Indian business and aviation news.
